nouns.explanation: A piece of land with water all around it.
Another word for an island, often used in stories and poems.
A very small island.
A ring-shaped island made of coral.
A group of many islands.
The large mass of land that islands lie near.
The edge of the land all along the sea.
A small beach tucked in between rocks or cliffs.
A calm pool of sea water, cut off from the open sea.
A long line of rock or coral just under the sea.
A hard, colourful substance in warm seas, made by tiny sea animals.
The tops of cliffs.
A piece of high land that sticks out into the sea.
Tall trees with large leaves only at the top, found in hot places.
The long, feathery leaves of a palm or fern.
A thick, hot forest.
The inside part of an island, away from the coast.
A mountain that can throw out fire, smoke and melted rock.
A sheltered place where boats can stay safely.
The places where boats are tied up.
A wooden or stone platform that sticks out into the water.
A tall tower with a bright light to warn ships.
A long, low ridge of sand in the sea.
The part of the water that is not deep.
The routes across the sea that ships usually follow.
The line far away where the sea seems to touch the sky.
The slow rise and fall of the sea.
Thick cloud close to the ground or sea.
Birds that live near the sea.
A stone platform beside the water where boats load and unload.
Large groups of fish swimming together.

adjectives.explanation: Very far away from other places.
With palm trees growing along the edge.
A bright colour between blue and green.
Full of bright colour and life.
Fresh and green with growing plants.
Beaten again and again by storms.
With mist curling all around it.
Burning slowly, with smoke but no flame.
Old, shaky and likely to break.
As brightly coloured as a jewel.
Most common. The prevailing wind is the one that blows most often.

verbs.explanation: Shone with a soft, wavering light.
Went all the way round something.
Hit hard and fast, like a whip.
Moved slowly from side to side.
Touched something softly again and again, like small waves.
Protected something from the wind and waves.
Made a home in which to lay eggs.
Made a loud, harsh, high cry.
Played in water so that it flew about.
Floated on the water. A ship rides at anchor.
Made a long, deep, rolling sound.
Was full of living, moving things.
Moved a boat along with oars.

verbs.text: Lay far beyond the shipping lanes
Rode at anchor in the bay

sentences.text: The tiny, palm-fringed island shimmered on the horizon like a mirage that refused to fade.
The island rose out of the sea like the back of some vast, sleeping creature.
Encircled by a coral reef, the still, turquoise lagoon lay as calm as a held breath.
The remote, uninhabited island lay far beyond the shipping lanes, and no sail ever broke its horizon.
Battered by Atlantic gales, the bare, storm-lashed islet could not hold a single tree.
Tall, slender palms swayed in the warm breeze, their fronds whispering like rain.
They waded ashore onto a pristine, white beach that showed no footprint but their own.
Dark, forbidding cliffs loomed out of the fog, and the captain bellowed for the ship to turn.
A long headland jutted into the sea and sheltered the harbour from the prevailing wind.
The sleepy fishing harbour drowsed in the afternoon heat, its boats nodding at their moorings.
Small waves lapped beneath the planks of the rickety, wooden jetty.
Raucous, jewel-bright parrots screeched in the treetops.
Children splashed in the shallows, chasing shoals of tiny fish through the warm, crystalline water.
Dense, impenetrable jungle cloaked the interior, right down to the edge of the sand.
The ship dwindled to a speck and was gone, leaving them alone with the vast, indifferent ocean.
Mountainous, storm-driven waves lashed the coast and flung spray clean over the clifftops.
A single fishing boat rode at anchor in the bay beneath the low, green hills.
Beneath the surface, the vibrant coral reef teemed with life, every crevice flickering with colour.
The smouldering, black volcano rumbled in the distance, and the ground shivered beneath their feet.
Thousands of seabirds nested on the cliffs, and their clamour carried a mile out to sea.
The solitary, white lighthouse stood at the island's tip, flashing its warning to an empty sea.
Jagged, hidden reefs lay just beneath the swell, patient as teeth.
At low tide, a long, narrow sandbar emerged to join the two islands like a pale bridge.
They rowed into a small, rocky cove on the sheltered side of the island.
For three days the storm raged, and the sea pounded the island from every side as if determined to drown it.
The island basked in sunshine, and nothing stirred but the palms and the slow, glassy swell.
Strange cries drifted from the trees of the mysterious, mist-wreathed island.
He stood on the deserted shore each evening, searching the horizon for a sail that never came.
Turtles hauled themselves up the beach by night to bury their eggs in the sand.
The market on the quay was a riot of colour: mangoes, bright cloth, and fish still flapping in their baskets.
